newsitem.title: UK: Euro shares move ahead, dollar slips back.
newsitem.headline: Euro shares move ahead, dollar slips back.

text.p: European shares extended their recent gains on Thursday, although caution ahead of the Easter holiday break held the Frankfurt bourse in check.

Wall Street gave little lead, slipping a little in early trading along with bonds after U.S. February home sales figures were higher than forecast -- suggesting strength in the economy which could eventually prompt a further rise in interest rates.
On the currency market the dollar drifted lower, as thin pre-holiday trading exaggerated movements, but later recovered from its lows.
"There's actually not much trade going through in spite of the price moves. That didn't take more than just a few major sellers," said a currency trader at a German bank.

Traders in London, the biggest European stock market, reported pre-holiday caution amid uncertainty over higher interest rates and the British election campaign. The market will be closed on Friday and Monday.
Up to mid-afternoon shares were, however, underpinned by higher bond prices and by "bed and breakfast" tax-related trading near the end of the fiscal year on April 5.
"We've seen a lot of bed and breakfast deals this morning," one senior dealer said. "Market makers are also trying to squeeze out a few bears ahead of the (tax) year end."
Bed and breakfast transactions, which involve selling shares and then immediately buying them back ahead of the end of the tax year, are used to book capital gains or losses for tax purposes.
But many market participants were absent ahead of the long Easter weekend break.
"Most dealing rooms aren't fully staffed. Some people have headed off early," one London trader said.
Market participants still at work were already fretting about the next tightening of American monetary policy after this week's quarter percentage point interest rate rise.
Analysts speculated that the Federal Reserve could boost U.S. rates again in May to keep a lid on inflation.
Pre-Easter caution curbed the enthusiasm of the German share market but interest in the car and financial sectors aided the blue-chip DAX index to a slightly higher close.
Stronger bond markets helped French shares revive after opening marginally weaker, with healthy company results giving support.
For the dollar, meanwhile, concern over Japan's large trade surplus and disappointment that it failed to gain more after Tuesday's rate rise were depressants.

"The dollar had a good go at the upside this week as a lot of people bought dollars ahead of the Fed meeting and the rate hike. Then nothing much happened afterwards so it's coming off a bit," said one trader at a U.S. bank in London.
The U.S. currency slipped against the yen in Asian business after concern expressed by U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers about Japan's trade surplus with the United States.
"The dollar's slipped a bit on the Summers comment but it's very quiet in Europe with the holidays beckoning," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Summers said Washington had frequently expressed concern about the "dangerous possibility" that the Japanese current account surplus would expand substantially.
Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin will visit Japan on April 4 for talks in which the nagging trade tensions are expected to feature prominently.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.6805 marks and 123.70 yen, compared with 1.6920 and 124.16 in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 17.3 points, or 0.40 percent, at 4,318.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was 19.54 points or 0.74 percent ahead at 2,668.27.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade up 10.93 points, or 0.32 percent, at 3,429.05 but slipped nearly four points from this level in later electronic trading.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $348.15 an ounce in the afternoon, down from the morning fix of $349.50 and previous London close of $348.75 amid light selling. Silver was three cents weaker at $5.12.
